title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
event_hint: Research paper presents SPDP, a unified sparse-inference framework for LLM inference
problem: Autoregressive decoding in LLMs suffers from computational and memory bottlenecks. Existing weight pruning methods are confined to either static pruning (permanent but lacks input adaptivity) or dynamic pruning (adaptive but introduces runtime irregularity and coarse-grained masks)
mechanism: SPDP unifies unstructured static pruning with input-adaptive dynamic pruning through co-designed Tiled-Column-wise Bitmap Compressed (Tiled-CBC) format and two GPU kernels: (1) CUDA-core spMspV kernel with Hybrid Activation-aware Dynamic Shared-Memory Bitmap Decoding (HAD-SMBD) for fine-grained activation skipping, and (2) Tensor-Core SpMM kernel for prefill computation. Static and dynamic pruning act on orthogonal dimensions (row-wise vs column-wise), multiplying effective sparsity

evidence.claim: SPDP achieves 1.24x-1.37x average kernel speedup over state-of-the-art SpInfer framework, with maximum up to 2.51x
evidence.condition: Inference-optimized GPUs (A10G, L4), moderate sparsity range 30-50%

evidence.claim: SPDP spMspV kernel achieves 1.88x average speedup over dense cuBLAS baseline on A10G GPU
SPDP spMspV kernel achieves 2.11x average speedup over cuBLAS on L4 GPU
End-to-end evaluation on LLaMA-2-7B shows SPDP achieves higher average TPOT speedup (×1.34) than SpInfer at comparable sparsity while maintaining lower perplexity (under 5.4)
evidence.condition: LLaMA-2-7B-hf model, end-to-end decode latency measurement

evidence.claim: SPDP achieves higher SM utilization (48.0% vs 38.2-48.0%) and fewer bank conflicts (74 vs 3817) compared to SpInfer

evaluation_context: Kernel-level evaluation on A10G and L4 GPUs using representative matrix shapes from major LLM architectures (OPT 13B-175B, LLaMA-2 7B-70B, LLaMA-3 8B/70B, Qwen 7B/14B/72B, Mixtral-8×7B, Phi-2/3, gpt-oss). End-to-end evaluation on LLaMA-2-7B-hf model across A10G, L4, and L40S GPUs. Focus on practical sparsity range of 30-50% for both static and dynamic pruning
limitations: Performance gains are constrained by memory-bound nature of decoding workloads and Amdahl-style upper bound from non-sparsity-sensitive operations (attention, normalization). Quantization and unstructured sparsity do not provide multiplicative compression in practice. Evidence limited to moderate sparsity regime (30-60%) typical for large LLMs; extreme sparsity (70-90%) not evaluated as it causes pronounced quality loss in large models
project_relevance: Directly relevant to AI infrastructure horizontal tracking: addresses GPU kernel efficiency and runtime optimization for LLM serving. Provides concrete system mechanism (unified static-dynamic pruning), performance-per-watt improvements, and engineering boundary (30-50% sparsity range for large LLMs). Should be categorized under 'serving_runtime_compiler' direction
